subject: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — mitigation & next steps
body:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@opticretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-01T08:14:00Z
Subject: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — mitigation & next steps

Hi Jenna / Tom,

I wanted to reach you immediately with what we know and the steps we're taking. Starting ~07:45 UTC this morning one of the regional Dedicated GPU pools experienced sustained headroom exhaustion (concurrent scheduled jobs + sudden traffic spike from a customer migration) causing degraded throughput for a subset of tenants using reserved capacity in us-west-2. Your traffic hit the pool during the higher-concurrency window and you may have observed elevated latency and a small number of 503s.

What we've done so far (high level):
- Identified a scheduler regression that left several warm nodes in a non-accepting state during autoscaler churn.
- Pushed an emergency routing policy to divert new requests to spare pools in other zones for impacted tenants.
- Incrementally scaled up warm standby capacity and applied a hotfix to the autoscaler.
- Captured the timeline and debug logs; attaching the timeline and hotspot logs (see attachments).

Immediate impact for OpticRetail: brief latency increases between 07:45–08:05 UTC, >95th percentile tokens-per-second dipped by ~28% for your dedicated endpoints, and we saw ~0.6% error rate during the window.

Next steps and ask from us:
1) We will keep the temporary routing policy for the next 6 hours to allow traffic to normalize and run a controlled desaturation.
2) Our infra team will run a non-production replay against your representative workload to validate no behavioral regressions from the hotfix.
3) Monica will open a HubSpot ticket to document crediting and a follow-up postmortem call.

We will offer a goodwill credit equivalent to one week of committed Dedicated capacity for the impacted window; Monica will share details. I will follow up with a full postmortem (timeline, root cause, remediation, and protective guardrails) by EOD tomorrow.

Attachment stubs: (attachment: incident_timeline_20280901.csv) (attachment: hotspot_logs_08-31.zip)

I understand the disruption is unacceptable and we're treating this with priority. Please let me know if you want an immediate call — I can have engineering on the line now.

Best,
Michael Grant
Sr. Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

-----
From: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@opticretail.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@opticretail.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T08:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — mitigation & next steps

Thanks Michael — appreciate the quick update. Can you confirm whether the routing diversion changes our egress region or will it keep traffic in us-west? We have compliance constraints about regional egress for some PII-related inference calls. Also, ETA for the hotfix validation?

Would prefer a short call to confirm billing implications before Monica opens anything. Available 09:00–09:30 UTC.

— Jenna
Director, ML Platforms, OpticRetail

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@opticretail.com>
Date: 2028-09-01T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — mitigation & next steps

On 2028-09-01 at 08:14 Michael wrote:
> Starting ~07:45 UTC this morning one of the regional Dedicated GPU pools experienced sustained headroom exhaustion...

Quick technical note to clarify: the temporary routing policy preserves regional constraints — traffic is only routed to spare capacity within the same allowed region (us-west-2). We did not route outside customer-specified regions.

Root cause (summary): an autoscaler change from last week inadvertently left nodes in a terminating state while the scheduler marked them available; under a correlated ramp (a scheduled SOC job + unexpected client migration), the pool lost effective capacity. Hotfix details: we reverted the terminating-state detection threshold and applied a guard that prevents scheduler assignment to nodes in a transient state.

Validation plan: we will run a 60-minute replay test against a captured trace of OpticRetail traffic and monitor p95 latency, token throughput, and error rate. Expected completion time: 10:30 UTC. If the replay passes, we'll remove the routing diversion and let autoscaler operate normally with the guard in place.

Attachments: route_change_plan.patch (small patch + runbook)

Karthik
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@opticretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-01T10:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation — mitigation & next steps

Jenna — quick update after the validation run.
- Replay completed at 10:18 UTC. p95 latency and tokens/sec returned to baseline under the same simulated load.
- No regression observed in the mock PII-anchored flows; replay was run in-region (us-west-2).
- We removed the temporary routing diversion at 10:25 UTC and continued to monitor.

We still plan a full postmortem with timeline and preventative work (autoscaler guard, scheduler health probe, and extended warm-standby testing). Proposed time for a joint call to review findings and billing: 2028-09-02 15:00 UTC (30 minutes). Monica, please confirm slot and the credit paperwork.

(attachment: route_change_plan.patch)

Michael

Confirming the 2028-09-02 15:00 UTC slot for the postmortem call. Please include an ops-level slide deck or timeline in advance so our platform team can review.

— Jenna

Action items I have:

- Prepare a one-week equivalent credit proposal and alternate options (pro-rata vs fixed week).
- Share the postmortem draft and runbook links ahead of the meeting.

Thanks — Monica
